stories.title: 玻璃钥匙协议
stories.description: 一场黑色悬疑冒险：你在雨夜霓虹与加密档案之间追寻真相，而密室死亡不断被改写。每条线索都有代价，每个盟友都有价格，最终答案也许并非你能承受的那一个。
stories.author: FableFlow Studios

nodes.title: Rain on Glass
nodes.narration: You stand under the awning of the Glassward Hotel while rain needles the street and turns neon into bleeding watercolor. Inside, someone important is dead, and the building is already trying to pretend it never happened. The concierge told dispatch it was a heart attack; the coroner called it a locked-room anomaly; your chief called it a favor you cannot refuse. You taste ozone from a nearby transformer and the bitter coffee you should not have skipped. Through the lobby windows you catch reflections: bell staff moving too quickly, guests pretending not to stare, a security guard who watches you like a mirror watches a face. Your phone vibrates with a single text from an unknown number: 'Do not trust the first story.' The hotel looms, all polished stone and perfect angles, like it was designed to hide seams. You adjust your badge and feel the weight of it, like a coin that could buy truth or buy silence.

choices.text: Enter through the humming service corridor
Walk in openly, badge bright in hand

nodes.title: Back-of-House Whispers
nodes.narration: The service corridor smells of bleach, wet wool, and fried oil seeping from the kitchen vents. Your shoes squeak on tile as you pass carts draped with white sheets, each one shaped like it is hiding a secret. A dishwasher pauses, hands red and raw, and watches you without blinking. Above you, pipes tick like a slow metronome. A door marked STAFF ONLY is propped open with a fire extinguisher, and beyond it you see a narrow stairwell that climbs toward the suites. A young porter, barely old enough to grow stubble, blocks your path with a tray of untouched champagne flutes. His eyes are bright with rehearsed fear. He says the cameras on this level have been 'glitching all week,' but his mouth keeps tightening as if he is trying not to say a different word. When you ask who ordered the trays, he glances toward a utility closet with a keypad lock. You hear a soft electronic chirp from inside, like a device searching for a signal.

choices.text: Question the porter about the keypad closet
Slip upstairs before anyone can rehearse

nodes.title: The Lobby Performance
nodes.narration: The lobby is a stage built from marble and money. A chandelier throws prismatic shards across the floor, and every reflection looks like an edited version of the truth. Guests cluster in small islands of perfume and quiet laughter that breaks too sharply, like someone cueing applause. The concierge greets you with a smile that never reaches his eyes and offers a room key as if this is hospitality, not homicide. A security guard stands near the elevators, one hand on his radio, the other resting on nothing. You notice the guard's thumb tapping a rhythm, a nervous code. The concierge says the deceased is in a penthouse suite and that 'all access has been controlled,' which is a pretty way of saying someone has already decided what you should see. On the far wall, a digital art display cycles through serene ocean scenes, but the timing stutters, skipping frames like it is censoring something. When your phone reconnects to Wi-Fi, it immediately receives a file named GLASSKEY.aac, with no sender, no preview, just silence waiting to be played.

choices.text: Play the audio file beside the elevators
Demand the penthouse route and witnesses list

nodes.title: Keypad Breathing
nodes.narration: Up close, the keypad closet looks newer than the rest of the corridor, its paint too fresh, its screws too clean. The porter swallows and tells you the code changes daily and that only management and security have it. He says that like it is policy, but his fingers keep worrying the edge of his sleeve, shredding invisible threads. You press your ear near the door and catch a faint, rhythmic hiss, like a tiny fan cooling something that runs hot. A smell of warm plastic leaks through the seams. A single security camera is aimed slightly wrong, tilted toward the ceiling as if deliberately blinded. On the floor, near the baseboard, a smear of gray dust suggests something heavy was dragged recently, slow and careful.

choices.text: Force the door and photograph everything inside
Tail the porter toward whoever paid him

nodes.title: Stairwell to Silence
nodes.narration: The staff stairwell is narrow and loud with its own emptiness. Each step echoes like a confession. The walls are painted a tired beige that tries to erase memory, but you see scuffs at shoulder height, the marks of rushed bodies brushing past. Halfway up, you find a cigarette butt crushed into the landing, still damp from rain, which means someone came in from outside recently, not through the lobby. On the underside of the handrail, a strip of clear tape peels away, revealing a tiny fiber-optic thread that disappears into the wall. At the next landing, a door marked ROOF ACCESS is ajar. Cold air spills through, carrying the smell of tar and the metallic tang of distant sea. You hear footsteps above, light and quick, a person trying to move without being remembered.

choices.text: Push onto the roof and scan for movement
Follow the hidden fiber line toward suites

nodes.title: The Silence That Talks
nodes.narration: You press play. At first it is just ambient hotel noise: distant laughter, an elevator chime, the soft purr of ventilation. Then a breath, close to the microphone, as if someone leaned in to hide behind sound. A voice follows, calm and careful, speaking your name like it has practiced. It says, 'If you are hearing this, the room is already staged. Look for what does not belong to him.' The message ends with faint tones, like a handshake, then a click. The security guard is staring at you as if he heard it too. The digital ocean on the art wall stutters again, and for a blink you see a hallway camera feed with someone in a hooded coat entering an elevator with a slim hard case.

choices.text: Confront the guard about the altered display
Follow the elevator path from the skipped frame

nodes.title: Access, Controlled
nodes.narration: You demand names, times, and keys, and the lobby temperature seems to drop. The concierge hands you a witness list that is too clean, as if written for your convenience. It omits the positions that see everything. As you step toward the elevators, a woman in a soaked trench coat brushes past you and slips a hotel keycard into your palm. She whispers, 'Penthouse doors are honest. People are not.' The keycard has a room number that is not on the witness list.

choices.text: Accept the guard escort, watching his signals
Use the stranger keycard and avoid cameras

nodes.title: A Room That Watches Back
nodes.narration: The keycard opens a mid-level suite with blackout curtains and air that smells faintly of antiseptic. The room is immaculate except for one chair pulled slightly away from the desk, like someone left in a hurry but tried to erase the leaving. On the desk sits a compact audio recorder, its casing warm. Beside it, a single nitrile glove folded with care. In the bathroom mirror, a hairline crack catches the light like a scar, and the sink holds fine metallic filings. The Wi-Fi list shows an extra SSID, 'GK-PRIVATE,' stronger than the hotel's own. The room feels like a staging area, and you feel like you were meant to find it.

choices.text: Bag the recorder and trace the hidden SSID
Search the bathroom vents for planted devices

nodes.title: Rooftop Drift
nodes.narration: The roof hits you with wind and wet tar. Footprints in rooftop grime stop at an open maintenance hatch that exhales warm air. A coil of cable snakes toward a relay box beside a satellite dish, its seal broken. The blinking module inside pulses like a heartbeat. Farther along the parapet, a cigarette ember glows, then dies, as if someone watched you arrive and chose not to be seen. Your phone vibrates: 'They logged your entry already.' You realize the roof is not an escape route. It is a lens.

choices.text: Open the relay box and copy its module ID
Drop through the hatch to the wiring conduit

nodes.title: The Guard's Tells
nodes.narration: The security guard's jaw tightens when you mention the stuttering display. In the elevator, mirrored walls multiply you into a crowd. One button is physical, older: P-HOUSE. When you press it, you feel a faint vibration through the metal, not from movement, but from something else, a second system alive under the first. The guard says the deceased is Everett Caul, a donor darling with enemies. His earpiece is matte black, not hotel issue, and he answers his radio too fast, like he was waiting for the cue.

choices.text: Press the physical button again, feeling the vibration
Corner the guard with precise timeline questions

nodes.title: Penthouse Threshold
nodes.narration: The penthouse corridor swallows footsteps in thick carpet. Two doors stand at the end: one marked by discreet brass, the other unmarked and plain. A cordon tape blocks the marked door, applied crookedly, and you see a faint scuff near the lock. The camera above the corridor is off, but its indicator light is on, a contradiction that makes your skin prickle. The marked door feels cooler than the hallway, as if the room beyond is over-conditioned to preserve a scene.

choices.text: Enter the marked suite and document the scene
Test the unmarked door for hidden access routes

nodes.title: GK-PRIVATE
nodes.narration: You connect to GK-PRIVATE. It requires no password, which is its own arrogance. A blank page loads a tiny key icon. Your battery drains faster than it should, and encrypted bursts spike every time you move, like the building is tracking signal strength as location. The bagged recorder chirps with the same handshake tones from GLASSKEY.aac. Your phone pings with an IP address and a line: 'Room 1407 is not empty.' You understand someone wants you to open the wrong thing, at the right time.

choices.text: Go to room 1407 before the trail cools
Spoof your device identity and probe the portal

nodes.title: The Locked Room
nodes.narration: Inside the marked suite, Everett Caul lies on the carpet in a posture that looks almost composed. The window is sealed, the balcony door latched, and the room key sits in the lock, turned halfway as if interrupted. No sign of forced entry, but the room smells faintly of citrus and electrical heat. A luxury watch is missing from Caul's wrist, leaving a pale band. On the carpet near his hand, you find a glittering sliver of tempered glass, too fine to be from a window, shaped like it broke from a small screen.

choices.text: Photograph the glass sliver and check for residue
Inspect the lock and key for subtle tampering

nodes.title: Second System
nodes.narration: You pop the elevator maintenance panel and find a slim device taped inside, wired to the button circuitry with clean solder points. A tiny LED blinks in the same pattern as the handshake tones. You snap photos and copy the serial number: it begins with GK. You notice gray rooftop dust on your glove, the same grime you saw near the parapet. Someone moved between roof and elevator without public routes. Your phone buzzes: 'They can make you look guilty on video.'

choices.text: Take the device and risk triggering alarms
Leave it, but trace its signal source

nodes.title: The Conduit Route
nodes.narration: You follow a matte black cable through a maintenance shaft and into a crawlspace parallel to the penthouse corridor. Through drywall, you hear clipped security talk and then your chief's voice saying, 'We need this contained.' A junction box holds an audio transmitter, indicator steady. Someone is listening to the penthouse, and someone in your chain of command is part of it. Your phone receives: 'If you keep digging, you lose someone you love.'

choices.text: Record the voices and secure the transmitter
Back out silently and follow the black cable

nodes.title: Room 1407
nodes.narration: Room 1407 is cold like it is preserving something. A wall is covered in printed surveillance stills. Your face appears entering the lobby, stepping into the elevator, and leaving the penthouse corridor with a timestamp from an hour ago, a fabrication arranged like evidence. On the bed, a laptop runs a timeline editor labeled 'SCAPEGOAT CUT.' In the sink, gloves drip water tinted faintly gray, like they rinsed rooftop grime. Someone set this room to frame you, and they expected you to find it.

choices.text: Copy the laptop drive and wipe your fingerprints
Hide and wait for the editor to return

nodes.title: Identity Required
nodes.narration: You spoof your device identity and pull a file list: /GK/KEYS, /GK/CUTS, /GK/ROOMS, /GK/HEART. You extract a text file of room numbers and timestamps: 'PENTHOUSE 02:14 HK,' '1407 02:46 SC,' 'ELEVATOR P 02:10 IN.' The network floods your phone with junk traffic until it heats in your palm. A message appears: 'You are early. That is inconvenient.' Footsteps approach outside your door, followed by a keycard beep.

choices.text: Escape through the service stairs with the file
Confront the intruder and force a name

nodes.title: Tempered Truth
nodes.narration: The glass sliver suggests a small screen, tinted like privacy glass. Beneath Caul's jaw you spot a pinpoint bruise, consistent with an injection site. Adhesive dots under the nightstand suggest a device mount aimed at the bed. You imagine a stimulus delivered without force: an image, a sound, a shock, a chemical push. Your phone pings: 'The heart is programmable.'

choices.text: Search Caul's belongings for missing wearable data
Trace the injection clue to medical staff logs

nodes.title: Lockwork Lies
nodes.narration: The key teeth show micro-scratches consistent with rapid duplication. The lock cylinder holds a smear of lubricant applied to mask tampering. The latch plate has a hairline bend where a shim could slide. The peephole lens has been replaced with a wider angle. Your phone buzzes from a new number: 'Stop. You are walking into a cut.'

choices.text: Hide the key and set a trap at the door
Leave now and chase the master key holder

nodes.title: The Missing Watch
nodes.narration: Caul's missing watch is not vanity; it is data. A warm charging puck suggests it was removed recently. Caul's tablet shows notification previews: 'Cardiac variance detected,' and a calendar entry named GK CHECK-IN. A service cart sits near the elevator bank, linens stacked too square. Your phone receives an encrypted smartwatch export file titled 'EVERETT_LAST' from 'A friend of the truth.'

choices.text: Decrypt the export using your on-device tools
Inspect the linen cart for hidden medical gear

nodes.title: Clinic Smell in a Hotel
nodes.narration: The hotel's incident log shows a private nurse visit authorized by a vendor badge that does not exist in city records. You glimpse a hidden elevator menu: 'GK SERVICE MODE.' Your phone buzzes with a text from your sibling: 'Someone asked about you at my work. Should I be worried?' The timing feels engineered.

choices.text: Warn your sibling and set a meet point
Force open GK service mode on the elevator

nodes.title: A Trap in the Dark
nodes.narration: You set a subtle trap and wait. The lock turns and a gloved hand slips inside, wrist showing a thin GK tattoo. Then your chief's voice sounds in the corridor: 'Officer, step away from the scene.' You realize your chief is not just on the recordings. He is here, close, with someone who wants you caught in this moment.

choices.text: Surrender calmly, listening for hidden tells
Bolt through the service exit before cameras focus

nodes.title: Name at Knife-Point
nodes.narration: A figure with hotel clothing that sits too crisp steps in, showing a small remote. Your phone flashes: 'REMOTE WIPE REQUESTED.' The figure murmurs, 'Caul did not die for money. He died because he tried to keep a key.' Their wrist shows the GK tattoo, lines clean, no tremor.

choices.text: Disarm the remote before they can wipe
Feign compliance and bait them into explaining HK

nodes.title: High Stakes: Heart Data
nodes.narration: The watch export reveals heart rate spikes and a note field that should not exist: 'Stimulus delivered.' Your screen flashes 'INCOMING GEO-FENCE REQUEST.' The decrypted metadata reads: 'Operator: HK.' You understand HK is a signature on a weapon, and the hotel is trying to keep your evidence inside its walls.

choices.text: Extract the final seconds and store offline
Disable Wi-Fi and move evidence to paper notes

nodes.title: High Stakes: Linen Cart
nodes.narration: Inside the linen cart you find a medical cooler, a sealed syringe kit, and electrodes. A slim tablet shows a live dashboard of room numbers and biometric fields, including 'COMPLIANCE.' Your location blinks tagged 'SC.' A photo arrives: your sibling leaving work, a hooded figure behind them. The message reads, 'Stop prying or they vanish.' The dashboard shows 'Operator: HK.'

choices.text: Hide the kit and follow the approaching footsteps
Photograph the dashboard and send to a safe contact

nodes.title: High Stakes: Family Line
nodes.narration: You call your sibling and give them a crowded meet point by the ferry terminal. Signal drops and returns with a text: 'We heard that.' You realize the hotel can listen through hidden fibers and relays. You tell your sibling to turn off their phone and go analog. The line dies, and you fear you just gave your enemy a coordinate.

choices.text: Commit to the case and trace HK immediately
Leave the hotel and intercept your sibling first

nodes.title: High Stakes: GK Service Mode
nodes.narration: You force GK service mode. Menus appear: CAMERA ROUTE, ACCESS OVERRIDE, HVAC ZONES, and CUTS. CUTS lists prebuilt video timelines with toggles: 'Insert suspect entry,' 'Remove witness angle,' 'Add timestamp drift.' One timeline is yours. The elevator opens onto a maintenance floor labeled IT CORE. Your chief texts: 'Stand down. This is above you.'

choices.text: Enter the IT core and pull the source logs
Screenshot CUTS evidence and retreat to public floors

nodes.title: Pre-Climax: The IT Core
nodes.narration: Server racks blink like language. A floor plan shows moving dots, including one labeled with your badge ID. A terminal shows a command: 'EXPORT_CUT node:SCAPEGOAT.' Logs record: 02:10 handshake, 02:12 HVAC shift, 02:14 stimulus delivered, 02:16 camera splice, 02:46 scapegoat cut prepared. A note reads: 'If investigator continues, execute FAMILY LEVER.' The door clicks behind you and a voice says, calm, 'You are not supposed to be here alone.'

choices.text: Hide the drive and bluff your way out
Trigger an alarm to flood the room with witnesses

nodes.title: Pre-Climax: Evidence on Paper
nodes.narration: You go primitive and write room numbers, timestamps, and operator tags in a notebook. In a banquet hallway, your chief calls again: 'Leave now. If you stay, they will make you the murderer on every screen.' A soaked trench-coat woman appears and signals an emergency exit, then points toward gathering security. She offers a fork: escape with evidence, or step into confrontation to end it.

choices.text: Follow the trench-coat woman through the exit
Walk toward security and demand the operator

nodes.title: Pre-Climax: Footsteps to the Operator
nodes.narration: You confront a clinic-badged person pushing a cart. They say, 'HK is not a person. HK is a key-holder. We keep systems stable.' They ask if you want your family safe and gesture toward a service door, offering a meeting where you can 'learn the truth without becoming it.' Your phone shows your sibling's meet point with a red warning overlay you did not install.

choices.text: Go to the meeting room and negotiate hard
Refuse and tail them to the true control hub

nodes.title: Pre-Climax: Ferry Terminal Lights
nodes.narration: At the ferry terminal cafe, bright lights and noise feel like a shield until your phone call turns into an unfamiliar voice: 'You brought leverage to a public place. Brave. Inefficient.' A hooded figure enters and sits with back turned, waiting. You realize the cafe is a different stage. You can accept terms to protect your sibling or vanish into the crowd and set a counter-trap.

choices.text: Accept the call terms to protect your sibling
Use the crowd to vanish and set a counter-trap

nodes.title: Final Decision: The Meeting Room
nodes.narration: In a windowless meeting room, an operator slides a folder: stills of you with corrected timestamps and a confession template with your name. They say, 'We remove volatility. Everett Caul became volatile.' They claim Caul stole the Glass Key, a credential that can edit records across systems. The offer is simple: sign and your sibling walks away, or take the Glass Key and become a key-holder, protected and complicit. Refuse, and the system will write your ending without you.

choices.text: Sign the confession to save your sibling
Take the Glass Key and join the operators

nodes.title: Final Decision: Alarm and Chaos
nodes.narration: You trigger an alarm in the IT core. Sirens and red strobes fracture the hotel's calm. The trench-coat woman appears and urges you to steal the key. She points to a secure rack labeled GK HEART. She offers two routes: copy the key and broadcast logs to create too many witnesses to erase, or destroy GK HEART, cutting control but erasing evidence that could clear you.

choices.text: Copy the Glass Key and broadcast everything now
Destroy GK HEART to end their system forever

nodes.title: Final Decision: Terms in Public
nodes.narration: The voice on the line orders you back to the hotel and wants your sibling as leverage. The trench-coat woman slides a napkin with a key and an address: an old newspaper office. Outside, a van idles with lights off. Your phone receives an image of you in the hotel corridor, timestamped in the future. They are showing you they can prewrite you. You can go to the newspaper office and gamble on witnesses, or return to negotiate inside their rules to keep your sibling alive by staying predictable.

choices.text: Go to the newspaper office and seek witnesses
Return to the hotel and negotiate within their rules

nodes.title: Final Decision: Counter-Trap
nodes.narration: You vanish into the crowd, then set a five-minute mirror stream with a city IT friend. The hooded figure stops when you name HK, GK, and CUTS. Your friend texts, 'Stream ready. Say when.' Broadcast now and risk retaliation, or go quiet to protect your sibling and disappear tonight.

choices.text: Trigger the live stream and speak the whole timeline
Go quiet, prioritize family, and disappear tonight

nodes.title: Ending: The Confession Cut
nodes.narration: You sign. The pen feels heavier than it should, like it contains gravity. The operator watches without satisfaction, just confirmation, as if a checkbox finally turned green. They slide your signed page into the folder and tap a tablet. Somewhere, a story updates. You are escorted out through a hallway that avoids cameras, because they do not need cameras anymore. They already have footage, edited and timed, waiting for release. Your sibling calls you thirty minutes later from a blocked number, voice shaking but alive. They say someone drove them home and told them to sleep, told them everything would be fine if you stayed 'cooperative.' You tell them you are fine too, because lies are contagious and you are saving them from the truth the only way you can. In the morning, the news runs a clean headline: 'Officer Arrested in Hotel Death.' The video is perfect. Your face is in the wrong places at the right times. The timestamps align. The city believes it because it is easier than believing a hotel can rewrite reality. Your chief does not call. Your badge is revoked. Your case file becomes sealed, then lost. Weeks later, you receive a package with no return address: a luxury watch, Everett Caul's, wiped clean. The screen lights once, showing a single message in thin text: 'Stability restored.' You stare at it until the battery dies. You saved your sibling. You lost the truth. And you realize that the Glass Key did not just open doors. It locked them from the inside.

nodes.title: Ending: The Key-Holder's Coat
nodes.narration: You take the Glass Key, and the world shifts subtly, like your eyes adjusted to darkness you did not know was there. The operator does not smile, but their shoulders relax, as if you removed a risk from the room by becoming part of its structure. They give you a new phone, a new credential, and a simple rule: never use the key for ego. Use it for stability. You think of Everett Caul and feel a dull ache of respect and disgust braided together. Within hours, the city's narrative changes. The hotel death becomes a private medical tragedy. Your presence at the scene vanishes from public camera feeds. Your badge returns without paperwork. Your chief calls with relief in his voice that sounds like guilt set down, and he says only, 'Good. You understand now.' Your sibling remains safe, untouched, but they stop asking questions, as if someone gently discouraged curiosity. You spend nights learning the system: how CUTS can remove a person from a timeline, how HVAC shifts can shape behavior, how a stimulus can push a heart into a story it cannot refuse. You tell yourself you will use the key to stop worse outcomes, to prevent chaos, to protect the innocent. And sometimes you do. But you also learn the seductive power of editing. One small deletion makes life easier. One inserted timestamp fixes a problem. One quiet cut removes a complication. The key teaches you that truth is expensive and stability is cheap. Months later, a message arrives on your secure channel, tagged HK: 'Welcome. Your first assignment: erase the man who keeps texting you.' You recognize the phrasing. It is the voice that warned you at the start. The friend of the truth. You stare at the cursor, realizing you have become the locked room, and the door only opens if you choose who gets to breathe.

nodes.title: Ending: Broadcast Under Rain
nodes.narration: You trigger the live stream. The five-minute window opens like a lung. You speak fast and specific: rooftop relay, elevator device, GK service mode, CUTS menu, operator HK, stimulus delivered, scapegoat cut prepared. Your friend's mirror server throws it outward to platforms GK does not fully control. For a moment, the city sees the seams. Screenshots multiply. Journalists begin calling, hungry and terrified. The system tries to erase you mid-sentence, but it is too late. Witnesses exist now, and witnesses are the enemy of edited truth. The hotel goes into lockdown. Your chief screams for you to stop, which confirms everything. You reach your sibling as a van door opens nearby and you shove them into the bright cafe with other people, forcing the world to look. The van retreats, unwilling to abduct on camera. The next day, denials and leaks collide. A high-ranking official tied to private security partnerships resigns suddenly. You are suspended, then offered protection for silence. You refuse. You cannot go home, and you cannot trust perfect footage anymore, but the story is no longer theirs alone. Everett Caul's death becomes a key that opens public eyes, and you learn truth does not save you. It only gives you a reason to keep moving.

nodes.title: Ending: Burn the Heart
nodes.narration: You choose destruction. You rip open the GK HEART rack and smash the core module until sparks spit and cameras freeze. Elevators halt. The system loses its language. Outside, rain hits your face like baptism. The city cannot get a neat confession video now, because GK can no longer render it. But you also lose clean proof that could clear you forever. In the following weeks, traffic cameras glitch, municipal records show errors, and private clinics shut down quietly. Nobody announces GK's death. They pretend the failures are coincidence, because admitting the truth would require admitting the control. Your chief disappears from public view. Your sibling stays safe, but you both live with fear of what survives when a hidden machine breaks. You stopped the heart, but the body is still moving, and you do not know what it will do when it finally realizes it can bleed.

nodes.title: Ending: The Newspaper Witnesses
nodes.narration: You go to the old newspaper office where the air still smells like ink. The trench-coat woman meets you and gives a usable name: Mara. In a back room, archivists mirror and package your evidence through time-delayed drops. Everett Caul came to them first, terrified, carrying partial keys and biometric exports. GK found him before the exposure could happen, and Caul left crumbs to you because you refuse convenient endings. The first drop goes live at dawn. It teaches the public how to look for edits and makes citizens suspicious of perfect footage. GK responds with threats and smear campaigns, but smear needs control, and control fractures when too many eyes are trained on the seams. Your sibling stays under watch, protected by publicity. You do not get justice in court. You get something slower: a city learning to doubt the first story. You stand in the old newsroom and listen to the rain, knowing Caul died trying to buy witnesses, and you keep the presses running so the next locked room does not stay locked.

nodes.title: Ending: Quiet Reconstruction
nodes.narration: You choose silence, not surrender. You cut power to every device you control and walk your sibling home through bright streets and crowded corners, keeping them inside other people's eyes. You do not go back to the hotel. You do not trigger streams. You do not negotiate. You disappear from the story long enough to keep your family intact. Over the next weeks, you rebuild the case in fragments: receipts, witness habits, analog notes, and a single copied serial number that begins with GK. You file nothing official. You speak to no one in command. You learn which cameras in the city run on independent systems, which storefronts keep unclouded backups, which old security firms never upgraded to the network GK owns. Your sibling stays safe, but they start locking doors twice and checking shadows in windows. One night, a plain envelope appears under your door with no stamp. Inside is a photo of you in the hotel lobby, timestamped yesterday, even though you were nowhere near it. A message is written on the back in thin block letters: 'We can still write you.' You do not panic. You do not rush. You take the photo to a local reporter you trust, not for publication, but for custody. You seed your evidence across people who do not know each other, turning your life into distributed storage. Months later, an audit scandal breaks in a different city, then another. No one says GK, but you recognize the pattern: the machine coughing after a hidden injury. You never get to announce a victory. You only get to keep living, holding the truth like a small warm coal in your pocket, waiting for the moment it can safely become fire.
